title: Straža Hill
paragraphs: A small ski slope in winter and a walking destination in warmer seasons. Seasonal summer activities may operate at the top.

title: Ojstrica, Osojnica & Kozarca
paragraphs: Three hills above the lake with memorable views of Bled, the Karavanke and Mt Stol. Choose a viewpoint walk that fits your ability; paths are steep in places. The pin marks Ojstrica.

title: Vintgar Gorge
paragraphs: Wooden walkways and bridges follow the Radovna River through a dramatic limestone gorge to a waterfall. Check seasonal opening, entry arrangements and the return route before going. The pin marks the gorge, not its entrance.

title: Mostnica Gorge & Voje
paragraphs: A beautiful walk through the gorge and towards the Voje valley, with a waterfall farther up the valley.

title: Pokljuka → Uskovnica
paragraphs: Drive to Pokljuka (Rudno Polje), park and hike to Uskovnica through forests and mountain meadows with cows and traditional cheesemaking. Look out for local dairy products and stop at a mountain hut for local food. Allow about 1 hour of easy walking each way.

title: Pokljuka → Lipanca
paragraphs: Hike uphill from Pokljuka to Blejska koča na Lipanci, a mountain hut with alpine scenery and traditional food. Allow about 1.5 hours uphill.

title: Vrata Valley
paragraphs: One of the great glacial valleys below Triglav. Visit the Slovenian Alpine Museum in Mojstrana and Peričnik Waterfall on the way. The pin marks Aljažev dom, near the head of the valley.

title: Peričnik Waterfall
paragraphs: An impressive waterfall reached via a forest path. The path can be slippery or icy, particularly in winter.

title: Mount Triglav
paragraphs: Slovenia’s highest mountain. We suggest a two-day climb with a night in a hut and a sunrise summit. The upper routes are exposed, demanding alpine terrain: go only with proper experience, equipment and conditions, ideally with a qualified guide.

title: Valley of the Seven Lakes
paragraphs: A classic route through the Julian Alps and the Triglav Lakes Valley. We suggest 2–3 days; a very long one-day outing is only for exceptionally fit, experienced hikers. The pin marks Koča pri Triglavskih jezerih.

title: Bohinj Valley
paragraphs: The map shows a suggested driving loop from Bled via Pokljuka (Goreljek), Bohinjska Češnjica, Studor, Stara Fužina, Lake Bohinj and the lower Vogel gondola station, returning via Bohinjska Bistrica. Walks to Mostnica and Voje and the gondola ride are separate, not part of the driving line. Stops are not confirmed parking spaces; check seasonal access and local restrictions.
If you have your own car, drive up to Pokljuka plateau with an amazing old pine forest and drive down to Bohinj Lake.

Buses connect Bled and Bohinj. Check the current timetable and nearest stop before travelling.
The traditional villages Studor, Stara Fužina and Češnjica are worth a visit.
Mostnica Gorge and Voje Waterfall are a great 2–3-hour walk.
Bohinj Lake is amazing — you can rent a boat, swim or hike around.
Vogel: take a gondola up to Vogel. You can do some hiking at the top; the views are amazing. It is a ski resort in the winter, has some nice restaurants (simple), a zip line and a chairlift for the hikes in the summer.

title: Radovna and Krma Valleys
paragraphs: The map shows a suggested out-and-back driving route from Bled via Gorje and the Radovna Valley to the road near Lake Kreda, Pr’ Psnak and Kovinarska koča in Krma Valley. Lake access is on foot from the road, not a drive into the lake. This is not a verified cycling route. Check road access, parking and local restrictions before travelling.

You will need a car or a bike for this trip. From Bled, go to Gorje village in the direction towards Pokljuka. At the end of the village, turn right and you come to the River Radovna. Then just follow the river upstream.
Lake Kreda
Lake Kreda is a possible stop in the valley. Check local access, swimming conditions and any restrictions before entering the water.
River Radovna
River Radovna is a crystal-clear river (also very cold) that is a source of drinking water for Bled and surrounding villages.
Pr’ Psnak
A homestay and a nice family restaurant with fresh, traditional homemade food.
Kovinarska koča
Kovinarska koča is a mountain hut located in Krma Valley. From here you have a great starting point for our highest mountain → Triglav.
The food is nice, simple and homemade.

title: Mojstrana and Vrata Valley
paragraphs: The map shows a suggested out-and-back driving route from Bled to the Slovenian Alpine Museum in Mojstrana, the roadside hut below Peričnik and the road near Aljažev dom in Vrata Valley. The waterfall walk is separate, not a driving section. The route uses the A2 motorway: check vignette requirements. Check seasonal vehicle restrictions, parking and any shuttle arrangements in Vrata; the line is not permission to drive to the hut.
Mojstrana
You can prolong your trip and visit Mojstrana village. It is a nice traditional Slovenian village with an Alpine Museum at the entrance to Vrata Valley.
Peričnik Waterfall
Peričnik Waterfall is near the beginning of Vrata Valley. A forest path leads towards the waterfall; some paths pass behind the falling water.
Paths can be slippery, icy or closed, especially in winter. Check local conditions and signs, and do not enter closed paths.
Vrata Valley
Vrata Valley is one of the three glacier valleys under Mount Triglav (Vrata, Kot, Krma). It is 10 km from Mojstrana village and brings you to the foot of the north wall of Triglav (1,000 m high).
Aljažev dom is a mountain hut at the end of the valley.

title: Planica & Tamar Valley
paragraphs: See the famous ski-jumping area and walk into Tamar Valley.

title: Gostilna Union
paragraphs: A grill close to the apartment. Check opening hours before heading over.

title: Pizzeria Rustika
paragraphs: Our pizza recommendation in Bled. Check opening hours before heading over.

title: Grajska plaža
paragraphs: Lakeside dining in the Bled swimming area. Open seasonally; check before you go.

title: Oštarija Peglez’n
paragraphs: A restaurant near Lake Bled. Check opening hours before heading over.

title: Pub Kitchen
paragraphs: A pub with food in the centre of Bled. Check opening hours before heading over.

title: Restaurant 1906
paragraphs: Higher-end dining overlooking Lake Bled. We recommend reserving a table.

title: Kovinarska koča
paragraphs: A mountain hut in Krma Valley with simple homemade food. Check opening before you go.

title: Pr’ Psnak
paragraphs: Traditional homemade cooking in the Radovna and Krma area. Check opening before you go.

title: Tonkina koča
paragraphs: A mountain hut known for its homemade food. Check opening before you go.

title: Slovenian Alpine Museum
paragraphs: Discover mountaineering history in Mojstrana.

title: Aquapark Bohinj
paragraphs: An indoor swimming option in Bohinjska Bistrica.

title: Ask the locals
paragraphs: Locals are happy to help with advice or directions.

title: Postojna Cave
paragraphs: A famous cave experience with guided visits. A day trip from Bled; book tickets in advance.

title: Škocjan Caves
paragraphs: Spectacular UNESCO-listed caves; a longer day trip from Bled. Book tickets in advance.

title: Tipping
paragraphs: Tips are welcome when service has been particularly good.

title: Drinking water
paragraphs: Tap water around Bled is generally drinkable, so carry a reusable bottle. For mountain trips, bring your own water.

title: Indoor swimming & wellness
paragraphs: Several hotels around Bled have swimming pools. Ask them about access for day guests.

title: Around the National Park
paragraphs: The map shows the suggested driving loop, with a dashed, schematic car-train connection from Most na Soči to Bohinjska Bistrica (not the exact railway track). Check road conditions and seasonal closures before travelling.
Full day — car necessary.
Route
Bled → Kranjska Gora → Vršič Pass → Trenta Valley → Bovec → Kobarid → Most na Soči → Bohinj → Bled.
This trip will take you around and through the National Park and Julian Alps.
Vršič Pass
Vršič Pass (1,611 m) is a scenic mountain road crossing. Expect steep gradients and tight hairpin bends; check weather and road closures before driving.
Trenta Valley
Trenta Valley is breathtaking. River Soča is crystal-clear, emerald colour.
Bovec
Bovec is a small town below Kanin mountain. Book outdoor activities with qualified local providers:

Rafting
Canyoning
Kayaking
Most na Soči — car train
Most na Soči has a car train taking you back to Bohinj through the tunnels in the mountains.

Check the current timetable, booking arrangements and capacity before relying on the car train. Arrive ahead of departure; service and space are not guaranteed. Plan a road alternative, for example via Soriška planina, and check conditions there too.

title: Trail maps
paragraphs: Take a photo of the map at the trailhead; it often helps on the way.

title: Before you go
paragraphs: Check route conditions, seasonal access and transport details before setting out.
